methods.label: Eliminate the vertical coordinates
methods.explanation:
Because both points lie on the line, \(b=ma+k\) and \(d=mc+k\). Subtracting eliminates the intercept \(k\), giving
\[
b-d=m(a-c).
\]
The distance formula, which follows from the Pythagorean theorem, now gives the distance \(L\) as
\[
\begin{aligned}
L&=\sqrt{(a-c)^2+(b-d)^2}\\
&=\sqrt{(a-c)^2(1+m^2)}\\
&=|a-c|\sqrt{1+m^2}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The absolute value is necessary because \(\sqrt{(a-c)^2}=|a-c|\), regardless of which horizontal coordinate is larger. If \(a=c\), the line equation also gives \(b=d\), and the formula correctly gives zero. Thus the answer is \(|a-c|\sqrt{1+m^2}\), choice A.
